to persuade, to prevail

examples.text: — И вы давно приняли христианство? — Нет, не очень давно… — Кто же вас убедил, — говорю, — в христианстве?

glosses: склонить к чему-либо, заставить согласиться на что-либо

examples.text: Он убедил робкого митрополита ехать к государю.

glosses: To make someone believe, or feel sure about something, especially by using logic, argument or evidence.

examples.text: I wouldn't have or do something, unless I'm convinced that it's good.
Such convincing proofs and assurances of it as might enable them to convince others.

glosses: To persuade.
To overcome, conquer, vanquish.

examples.text: […]his two Chamberlaines / Will I with Wine, and Waſſell, ſo conuince, / That Memorie, the Warder of the Braine, / Shall be a Fume,[…]

glosses: To behave believably in a role; to make someone perceive oneself as the character being portrayed.
To confute; to prove wrong.

examples.text: For hee mightily conuinced the Iewes, and that publikely, shewing by the scriptures, that Iesus was Christ.
And therfore, God neuer wrought Miracle, to conuince Atheiſme, becauſe his Ordinary Works conuince it.

glosses: To prove guilty; to convict.

examples.text: Which of you conuinceth mee of ſinne?
O ſeek not to convince me of a Crime / Which I can ne'er repent, nor can you pardon.

glosses: To successfully convince (someone) to agree to, accept, or do something, usually through reasoning and verbal influence.

examples.text: That salesman was able to persuade me into buying this bottle of lotion.

[VV]e are able with playne demonſtration to proue, and vvith reaſon to perſvvade that in tymes paſt our fayth vvas alike, that then vve preached thinges correſpondent vnto the forme of faith already published of vs, ſo that none in this behalfe can repyne or gaynesay vs.
We will persuade him, be it possible.

The boy became volubly friendly and bubbling over with unexpected humour and high spirits. He tried to persuade Cicely to stay away from the ball-room for a fourth dance. Nobody would miss them, he explained.

The most persistent tormentor was Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, who scored a hat-trick in last month’s corresponding fixture in Iceland. His ability to run at defences is instantly striking, but it is his clever use of possession that has persuaded some shrewd judges that he is an even better prospect than Theo Walcott.

glosses: To convince of by argument, or by reasons offered or suggested from reflection, etc.; to cause to believe (something).

examples.text: But beloued, wee are perswaded better things of you, and things that accompany saluation, though we thus speake.

glosses: To urge, plead; to try to convince (someone to do something).

examples.text: […] and hearken not vnto Hezekiah, when hee perswadeth you, saying, The Lord will deliuer vs.
She did not go into the coffee-room, though repeatedly persuaded by Miss Woodley, but waited at the door till her carriage drew up.
He persuaded me to go home, but I refused.
He did not persuade me long before I consented.

glosses: To be superior in strength, dominance, influence, or frequency; to have or gain the advantage over others; to have the upper hand; to outnumber others.

examples.text: Red colour prevails in the Canadian flag.
And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed; and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
Liverpool created a host of chances and had a Joel Matip goal ruled out for a foul and offside in an incident-packed game that went right down to the wire before Jurgen Klopp's side prevailed.

glosses: To triumph; to be victorious.

examples.text: There are a number of SCPs and tales that look at potential apocalypses, but rarely with such totality as SCP-2935, a parallel dimension in which death prevailed.

glosses: To be current, widespread, or predominant; to have currency or prevalence.

examples.text: In his day and age, such practices prevailed all over Europe.

glosses: To succeed in persuading or inducing.

examples.text: I prevailed on him to wait.
Jones began to be very importunate with the lady to unmask; and at length having prevailed, there appeared not Mrs Fitzpatrick, but the Lady Bellaston herself.

glosses: To avail.
Forzar o persuadir a otra persona con argumentos y pruebas a que piense o proceda de acuerdo con éstos.

examples.text: Convence a tus amigos para que vayan a clase.
